script:
HELO c.test
MAIL FROM:<alice@example.test>
RCPT TO:<@relay.example.test:bob@example.test>
QUIT

HELO c.test
MAIL FROM:<@origin.example.test:alice@example.test>
RCPT TO:<bob@example.test>
QUIT

a1 LOGIN bob bob-secret
a2 LOGOUT

HELO c.test
MAIL FROM:<alice@example.test>
RCPT TO:<@relay.example.test,@relay2.example.test:bob@example.test>
QUIT

provenance.oracle: RFC 2821 4.1.2, the @host,@host:user@domain form; same derivation as smtp.source.route.rcpt.flip (flip of the step-1 postfix-3.7.11 accept)
provenance.derivation: this ticket already requires 501 for both source-route forms; only the single-hop form was scored

provenance.oracle: RFC 2821 4.1.2, the @host,@host:user@domain form; same derivation as smtp.source.route.mail.flip, including the recorded follow-on 503 for RCPT with no accepted MAIL
provenance.derivation: this ticket already requires 501 for both source-route forms; only the single-hop form was scored

script:
HELO c.test
MAIL FROM:<alice@example.test>
RCPT TO:<@relay.example.test:bob@example.test>
RCPT TO:<bob@example.test>
QUIT

provenance.oracle: source-route 501 as in smtp.source.route.rcpt.flip, then the recorded postfix-3.7.11 RCPT TO:<bob@example.test> 250 (m01 smtp.rcpt.bob, recorded 2026-09-04T00:01:49Z)
provenance.derivation: RFC 2821 4.1.1.3: a rejected RCPT does not end the mail transaction, so the following valid RCPT still gets its recorded 250
